name: Point-Bench
intro: Point-Bench 是 PointArena 的静态语言引导指向基准，包含五类共 982 组图文任务。数据通过三个匿名多模态模型与人工评审筛选高难查询，再由 SAM 辅助生成并经两轮人工标注核验目标掩码；模型以坐标点覆盖掩码并按二元 Success Rate 评分。
org: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI, Anderson Collegiate Vocational Institute
build_method: 众包查询, 模型难度过滤, SAM辅助掩码, 双阶段人工复核
task_type: 点位预测, 空间推理
eval_feature: 5类任务, 3模型高难筛选, 掩码覆盖判定, 16个MLLM, 3次独立运行
build_method_en: Crowdsourced queries, model-based hardness filtering, SAM-assisted masks, two-stage human review
eval_feature_en: Five categories, three-model hardness filter, mask-coverage criterion, 16 MLLMs, three independent runs
intro_en: Point-Bench is the static language-guided pointing benchmark in PointArena, with 982 text-image tasks across five categories. Three anonymized MLLMs and human judges filter for difficult queries, while SAM-assisted target masks receive two stages of human annotation and verification; coordinate predictions are scored with binary Success Rate by mask coverage.

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=source-stage paper-aligned bilingual Build Process, fixed-source provenance, public-release boundary, paper-to-code scoring boundary, license boundary, and the source-stage topology contract. Primary evidence is PointArena arXiv 2505.09990v2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09990v2; PDF SHA-256 f2b79d4f8656d18779adb8f84ba416a21b3153133410f8172aef2d33efa2c2f7). Code evidence is fixed to official GitHub commit 16dab315e6e401aab6160d3dc9bba5e9cbc636eb. Data evidence is fixed to official Hugging Face revision 77ec5dca697b25025e655e2ec34fd2207856924c. Point-Bench is the 982-pair static-image and ground-truth component of the broader PointArena suite; Point-Battle and Point-Act are not inserted into its build pipeline. The paper formalizes one example as RGB image I plus natural-language query q, with a model predicting K image-space coordinates and supervision supplied by K-star binary target regions. A prediction succeeds only when K equals K-star and every target region contains at least one predicted point. The construction begins from public-source images posted after the paper's stated 2025-04-20 cutoff. Category-suitable scene selection supports five task-driven categories: Spatial, Affordance, Counting, Steerable, and Reasoning. Steerable examples use PixMo images with an existing reference point and ask relative questions without explicit object names. The paper describes the set as evenly divided; the diagram keeps that paper statement in the main flow and places exact public-release counts in a dashed boundary rather than silently conflating them. Crowd-sourced annotators see sampled category images and freely write natural-language queries aligned with each category theme. Three anonymized MLLMs then predict answers for each draft, and human evaluators judge correctness. The acceptance gate is exact: keep a query only when zero or one of the three model predictions is judged correct; drafts with more than one correct model prediction are excluded. The paper does not disclose a separate ambiguity filter, so the former invented 'reject ambiguous prompts' step was removed. For retained queries, annotators use the same Gradio interface to place intended target points directly on the image. SAM generates initial masks from those points; annotators edit or remove portions before submission; a separate annotator group manually verifies that masks accurately reflect the user-generated queries. The flow does not invent an undisclosed adjudication rule or claim that every verification failure is corrected. The paper's final Point-Bench contains 982 image-query pairs with pixel-level target masks. Evaluation is zero-shot across 16 open and proprietary MLLMs. Each model receives the same 982 pairs in three independent runs. The standardized output is [x,y], while Molmo, Qwen2.5-VL, and Gemini retain their documented coordinate outputs or prompt conventions. Non-counting tasks request one point and keep only the first if extra points are returned. Counting tasks preserve multiple predictions. Paper scoring then applies the formal region-wise condition K=K-star and requires every target region to contain at least one predicted point. The reported metric is binary Success Rate, summarized by category and average with means and standard deviations over the three runs. Public-release evidence is deliberately separated. At revision 77ec5dca697b25025e655e2ec34fd2207856924c, data.json has SHA-256 eb747f8f9c6d1d880cb29a6c341d9854bcbc9a29d329f04503474cfb7b3bfdfa and exactly 982 entries: affordable 198, counting 196, reasoning 193, spatial 195, and steerable 200. The release spelling 'affordable' differs from the paper's 'Affordance'. selected_images.zip is an LFS object with SHA-256 a82914086ddcc28d33a90aebb707cb99a5e0d91af5beab4159384ac4e1e0b6e9 and declared size 1,236,114,977 bytes; selected_masks.zip is an LFS object with SHA-256 a2c93869e659df6ddce5966fa660f0d9058237ed5d261c0664ae683cd11e2ed8 and declared size 3,657,233 bytes. pixmo_metadata.csv has SHA-256 1e682d65b0ad4e3bdbb3d5b343ab18c4e7018a7d0479358d69aed51c8972bc0a. The fixed release contains one mask_filename per item, and all 196 counting records carry a count field. Paper-to-code boundary: model_evaluator.py checks the predicted count and tests whether every predicted point lies anywhere inside that one loaded binary mask. It does not represent K-star masks separately or verify that each distinct target region receives a point, so it is not semantically identical to the paper's one-point-per-region coverage condition. The diagram therefore preserves paper scoring as the primary flow and shows this implementation difference only as a dashed boundary. The fixed code and HF card do not declare a dataset license and the Git tree has no LICENSE file; public access is not treated as an affirmative image or dataset reuse grant. The official project page presents a Point-Bench ranking table, therefore has_leaderboard is true. EN/ZH specifications have identical positioned topology, no edge labels, and dashed provenance edges. Strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; replacement formal assets and refreshed paper_aligned registration remain gated on independent reviewer approval.
